transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling, please?

Agent: Hello Rajesh, this is Priya from Lakshmi Finance. We're calling regarding your loan account ending in 4829. Your EMI of 12,500 rupees was due on the 15th of this month, and we haven't received the payment yet. Can we discuss this quickly?

Customer: Haan, I know, I know. Look, the thing is... <interruption> sorry, can you give me one minute? My wife is calling me from downstairs. One second, please.

Agent: Of course, take your time.

Customer: <pause> Okay, I'm back. Sorry about that. Look, Priya, the situation is very complicated right now. You see, I run a small textile business in Surat, and there was this massive flood in the city last month. The entire warehouse... everything got destroyed. Literally everything.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. That sounds very difficult. Can you tell me a bit more about what happened?

Customer: The monsoon rain was extremely heavy, and the water came into our warehouse at night. We didn't even know until morning. By that time, all the raw materials, finished stock, everything was soaked. We lost almost two months of inventory, which is about fifteen to twenty lakhs of rupees worth of goods. The insurance claim is still pending, and the assessor only came two weeks back.

Agent: That's a significant loss, Rajesh. I'm sorry to hear that. And your business operations... are you able to continue working?

Customer: That's the problem, Priya. We had to shut down for almost three weeks because we had no stock to work with. Even now, we are running at maybe thirty percent capacity. I had to take loans from relatives just to restart some operations and pay my workers' salaries. The business income has dropped to almost nothing compared to before. That's why I couldn't pay the EMI on the 15th.

Agent: I see. So the flood has directly impacted your business cash flow. Have you been able to make any partial payment since the due date?

Customer: No, nothing yet. I have been using every rupee to pay my workers and to buy even basic materials to restart. My bank account is running on empty, Priya. I am not refusing to pay you, but I literally cannot pay right now. The insurance claim should come through in the next two or three weeks, and once that happens, I will be able to clear everything, including the arrears.

Agent: Rajesh, I appreciate you explaining the situation. Can I confirm a few details? What is your current business address? Is it still in Surat?

Customer: Yes, yes, same location. But the warehouse itself is damaged and unusable. We are operating from a small rented space temporarily while the repairs are happening. The address is... let me think... it's Plot Number 42, Textile Park Extension, near Kadodara. But I'm staying at my home address most days now. You have my home address in the file, correct?

Agent: Yes, we have your residential address on file. And Rajesh, when you say the insurance claim should come in two to three weeks, is that a confirmed timeline from the insurance company?

Customer: The assessor visited and said the report would be ready within ten to twelve days. After that, it goes for approval, which should be another week or so. So yes, hopefully by end of next month, definitely by mid-month at the latest.

Agent: Understood. And Rajesh, just to clarify — this is a temporary situation caused by the flood, correct? Once the insurance payout comes through, your business and your ability to pay should recover?

Customer: Yes, yes, exactly. This is not a permanent problem. My business was doing well before the flood. Once I restart with new stock and the insurance money comes, everything will be normal again. I am not a defaulter by nature, Priya. This is just bad timing, bad luck.

Agent: I believe you, Rajesh. Given what you've described, we would like to help you through this difficult period. Let me escalate this to our hardship team. In the meantime, can you commit to making the payment once your insurance claim is processed? And do you have any amount you can pay in the next week or two, even as a partial payment?

Customer: I wish I could, but honestly, I don't have anything right now. Every rupee is committed. But once the insurance comes through, I will pay the full amount plus the arrears immediately. You have my word. And yes, please escalate it. I want to settle this properly.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh. I will escalate your case to our hardship and restructure team. They may contact you within the next two business days to discuss possible options. In the meantime, please try to get a written confirmation from your insurance company about the timeline, and share that with us when they call. That will help strengthen your case.

Customer: Okay, I will do that. And Priya, thank you for understanding. I was worried you would be aggressive or threatening like some collection agents I've heard about. I appreciate the empathy.

Agent: Of course, Rajesh. We understand that life sometimes throws unexpected challenges at us. Our job is to work with you, not against you. We'll be in touch shortly. Take care.

Customer: Thank you, Priya. I appreciate it very much. I will wait for their call.
Customer: The number you have dialled is currently switched off or out of coverage area.

Agent:Hello, good morning. Am I speaking with Mr. Vikram Singh?Customer:Yes, uhm... haan ji, this is Vikram.Agent:Mr. Singh, main Priya bol rahi hoon from FinSecure Bank. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account number ending in 9234. Your EMI of eighteen thousand five hundred rupees, which was due on the 7th of this month, is currently overdue.Customer:Oh, right, right. Yes, I know. Woh <interruption> Agent:Ji.Customer:Actually, thoda issue hai. My salary, you know, usually it comes by the 10th or 12th max, but this month na, it got slightly delayed. Abhi tak credit nahi hua hai, I was checking just yesterday only. Bas, isi ki vajah se thoda payment stuck ho gaya hai.Agent:I understand, Mr. Singh. So you're awaiting your salary credit. Do you have an estimate, roughly when you're expecting it? That would help us, you know, understand.Customer:Hmm, dekhiye, most likely by the 15th, 16th at the latest, it should be in my account. And then, once it's in, I'll need a day, maximum two days to clear the funds and make the transfer. So, uhm, can you please call me after the 16th? Say, 17th evening, like, 6:30 PM, is that okay? I'll definitely clear it then.Agent:Okay, understood, Mr. Singh. So just to reconfirm, you'd prefer us to call you back on the 17th of this month, around 6:30 PM? We will follow up on the overdue EMI of eighteen thousand five hundred rupees at that time. Is that correct?Customer:Yes, 17th, 6:30 PM, it will be perfect. Thank you so much for understanding, Priya.Agent:My pleasure, Mr. Singh. We'll schedule that callback for you. Please ensure the payment is made. Thank you for your time and cooperation. Have a good day.Customer:You too. Bye bye.

Agent: Hello, main [Company Name] se baat kar raha hoon Rajesh Sharma ji? Aapka account number PLX1234567 hai na? Hum aapko aapke personal loan ke overdue EMI ke regarding call kar rahe hain. Aapki pichli do EMIs Rs. 15,000 each, yaani total Rs. 30,000 aur late fees, overdue hain. Kya main jaan sakta hoon ki aap kab tak payment kar denge?
Customer: Haan ji, main Rajesh Sharma hi bol raha hoon. Pata hai mujhe, overdue hain. Main pichle kuch mahino se kaafi mushkil mein hoon sir, mera business na, theek se chal nahi raha hai. Kaafi losses hue hain COVID ke baad. Iss wajah se na, main yeh Rs. 30,000 abhi ekdum se nahi bhar pa raha hoon. Bohut pareshaani ho rahi hai.
Agent: Rajesh ji, hum samajh sakte hain aapki situation, lekin payment toh pending hai. Kya aap partial payment kar sakte hain? Ya koi chota amount, at least ek EMI ke barabar, pay kar dein?
Customer: Partial payment bhi bahut mushkil hai sir. Sach bolun toh meri itni capacity hi nahi hai abhi ki poore Rs. 15,000 bhi de paaon. Kya koi option nahi hai ki aap meri EMI thoda kam kar dein? Jaise Rs. 7,000 ya Rs. 8,000 kar dein kuch mahino ke liye? Aur jo late fees lagi hain na, woh bhi please waive off kar dijiye. Aur agar possible ho toh, tenure thoda extend kar do toh mere liye bohot rahat ho jayegi. Main koshish kar raha hoon business ko revive karne ki, but it's taking time.
Agent: Rajesh ji, aap EMI reduction aur late fees waive off ke liye keh rahe hain. Saath hi tenure extend karne ke liye bhi. Humare paas hardship policy hoti hai aise cases ke liye. Main aapki request system mein enter kar leta hoon aur apni team ko bataata hoon. Kya aap koi income proof ya bank statement submit kar sakte hain jo aapki current financial situation ko justify kare?
Customer: Ji, zaroor. Jo documents lagenge, main arrange karke de dunga. Bas kuch relief mil jaye. Aap please jaldi karwaye. Jab tak business normal na ho, main badi EMI nahi de paaunga. Aur yeh interest aur penalties toh bohot ho gayi hain.
Agent: Theek hai Rajesh ji. Main aapki request forward karta hoon. Hamari team aapko 2-3 working days mein wapas call karegi process batane ke liye. Aap humare website par bhi documents upload kar sakte hain agar chahein. Hum koshish karenge aapko jald se jald koi solution dene ki.
Customer: Haan ji, please kar dena. Main wait karunga call ka. Thank you.

Agent: Namaskar Ramesh Gupta ji, main Sunil bol raha/rahi hoon LegalServe se. Kya aapko hamare legal notice ki copy mili?
Customer: Haan bhaiya/behen, mili. Kal hi daak se aayi. Isliye main khud call karne wala/wali tha/thi.
Agent: Ramesh Gupta ji, gold loan account mein 18,000 rupees outstanding hai. Notice mein 15 din ka response time diya hai.
Customer: Ji jaanta/jaanti hoon. Maine apna lawyer se baat ki hai. Woh poori situation review kar rahe hain — loan agreement, calculation, sab. Hum proper reply bhejenge within timeline.
Agent: Theek hai Ramesh Gupta ji. Lawyer se respond karna bilkul appropriate hai. Sirf ensure karna ki 15 din mein response aaye.
Customer: Ji bilkul. Main cooperate karna chahta/chahti hoon, lekin sab kuch properly document hona chahiye.
Agent: Bilkul. Koi aur clarity chahiye toh call kar sakte hain.

Agent: Hello, mera naam Pooja hai aur main XYZ Bank se call kar rahi hoon. Kya main Mr. Ajay Sharma se baat kar rahi hoon?
Customer: Haan, main Ajay bol raha hoon. Kya baat hai?
Agent: Ajay ji, aapka personal loan account number XXXXXXX456 humare paas outstanding show kar raha hai, jismein Rs. 45,000 pending hai.
Customer: Arre, kaunsa account? Kya baat kar rahe ho aap? Maine toh woh loan already settle kar diya tha. Pichle saal hi September mein maine uska full settlement kiya tha!
Agent: Sir, humare records ke hisaab se aapka loan account abhi bhi active dikh raha hai aur Rs. 45,000 ki outstanding amount hai. Kya aapko koi confirmation ID ya reference number yaad hai us settlement ka?
Customer: Reference number toh abhi yaad nahi hai, but mujhe NOC bhi mili thi. Aap log baar baar call karte ho us loan ke liye jo main clear kar chuka hoon. Ye sahi nahi hai, main bahut pareshan ho gaya hoon in calls se.
Agent: Maafi chahta hoon sir agar aapko takleef hui hai. Lekin humare system mein abhi tak aapke settlement ka koi record nahi aaya hai. Kya aap confirm kar sakte hain ki aapne NOC kisse receive ki thi, matlab bank ki taraf se ya kisi collection partner se?
Customer: Bank ki taraf se hi mili thi! Maine payment bhi branch mein ki thi tab. Aap log pehle apne records theek se check karo, kyunki meri taraf se woh loan closed hai. Koi payment nahi karunga jab tak ye matter clear na ho. Maine toh socha tha loan band ho gaya hai, abhi tak phone kyon aa rahe hain?<interruption> Aap ek kaam karo, aapke team mein ya higher up kisi se baat karwao, kyunki aapke system mein toh galti hai.
Agent: Theek hai sir. Aapke issue ko hum yahan dispute mein mark kar rahe hain. Main ye matter apni senior team ko escalate kar rahi hoon takay woh aapke settlement records ko check kar sakein. Jab humein detail mil jayega, toh kya main aapko kal dopahar tak wapas call kar sakti hoon verification ke liye?
Customer: Haan, kar lena. Lekin please yeh baar baar calls mat karna jab tak aap confirm nahi kar lete ki mera settlement hai ya nahi. Jab NOC mili hai toh woh loan kaise active ho sakta hai! Mai dobara confirm karta hoon documents dhoond ke agar aapko email karna pada. Magar pehle aapki taraf se check karo.

Agent: Namaste, mera naam Priya hai aur main [Company Name] se baat kar rahi hoon. Kya meri baat Mr. Rahul Sharma se ho rahi hai?
Customer: Haan ji, main Rahul Sharma bol raha hoon. Kahiye.
Agent: Mr. Sharma, aapke loan account number jo 5678 par end hota hai, uski is mahine ki EMI Rs. 15,500, jo 5 May ko due thi, woh bounce ho gayi hai. Kya aapko iski jaankari hai?
Customer: Oh, haan, ji bilkul. Mujhe message aaya tha subah. Woh actually main balance daalna bhool gaya tha apne account mein, isliye woh bounce ho gayi. Bahut maafi chahta hoon uske liye.
Agent: Koi baat nahi Mr. Sharma. Toh, ab aap is EMI ko kab tak pay karwa sakte hain? Hum ise dobara process karne ka option de sakte hain.
Customer: Dobara process? Matlab wohi, ECS dobara lag jayega? Haan, woh theek rahega. Aaj toh main bahar hoon, toh balance load nahi kar paunga. Aap ek kaam kijiye, use parso ke liye schedule kar dijiye. Parso, yaani ki 9 May tak, main apne account mein sufficient balance rakh dunga.
Agent: Theek hai Mr. Sharma. Toh, hum aapke ECS mandate ko 9 May ke liye dobara present karwa denge. Kripya dhyan rakhiyega ki ek bounce charge bhi laga hoga aapke account par. Kya aapko woh manzoor hai?
Customer: Haan, haan. Bounce charge toh pata hai, lagta hi hai. Koi nahi, theek hai. Aap 9 May ko hi process karwa dijiye. Main balance rakh dunga.
Agent: Theek hai Mr. Sharma, confirmation ke liye main repeat kar rahi hoon, aapke loan account number 5678 ki EMI, Rs. 15,500, 9 May ko dobara process ki jayegi. Kripya us din apne account mein paryapt rashi banaye rakhiyega.
Customer: Ji, theek hai. Dhanyawad.
Agent: Dhanyawad Mr. Sharma. Aapka din shubh ho.

Bolo kaun?"Agent: "Namaste Mr. Sharma, main FinanceSecure Bank se Pooja bol rahi hoon aapke loan account number 4567 8901 2345 ke regarding. Aapki 35,000 rupaye ki EMI due thi 15 Tarikh ko, jo abhi tak receive nahi hui hai. Ussi ke bare mein baat karni thi."Customer: "Arre haan, Pooja ji. Pata hai yaar. Is baar toh life ki laga di hai, sach mein."Agent: "Arre sir, kya ho gaya? Kya problem ho gayi, batayenge?"Customer: "Mera jo job tha na, woh abhi chhoot gaya hai. Company loss mein chali gayi aur operations band kar diye. Ab 1st November se main jobless hoon. Bohot mushkil ho rahi hai, naye job ke liye interviews toh chal rahe hain, but kuch pakka ho nahi raha hai. Meri toh saari savings pe paani phir gaya isi chakkar mein."Agent: "Oh God, sun kar bohot bura laga, Mr. Sharma. Main aapki mushkil samajh sakti hoon. Lekin, aapko pata toh hai na sir, yeh loan aapki zimmedari hai. Kya aap koi part payment bhi nahi kar sakte abhi? Poora Rs. 35,000 ka amount pending hai."Customer: "Pooja ji, seriously bolun toh bank balance mein kuch bhi nahi hai. Ghar ke kharchon ka bhi pata nahi kaise adjust kar raha hoon. Next month ki salary aane ka toh abhi sawal hi nahi hai, jab job hi nahi hai. Meri priority abhi apne ghar ke kharche hain. Kuch akal hi nahi chal rahi hai, bohot stress mein hoon main."Agent: "Accha theek hai, Mr. Sharma. Agar aapko sach mein income mein dikkat ya job ka issue hai, toh hum definitely aapki help karne ka try kar sakte hain. Hum aapki problem samajh rahe hain. Hum isse hardship case mein consider karenge. Kya aapke family se kuch support mil sakta hai ya koi aur kaam dhandha mila hai?"Customer: "Nahi, abhi tak toh aisa kuch nahi hai Pooja ji. Main abhi bohot tension mein hoon aur jaan laga raha hoon nayi job dhundne ki. Agar aap thoda time de sakein ya koi solution nikal sakein toh bahut acha hoga."Agent: "Zaroor Mr. Sharma. Main aapki yeh situation ko apni team se discuss karti hoon ki kya relief ya restructuring ka option nikal sakta hai. Lekin, ek baat hai, aapko contact mein rehna padega, haan. Aur jaise hi aapko koi naya kaam ya paisa aane lage, turant bataiyega. Main aapko ek-do din mein call back karti hoon, theek hai? Options ke saath. Tab tak ke liye, apna dhyan rakhna. Kuch urgent hua toh please inform karna."Customer: "Haan, please call karna. Main definitely update karunga. Thank you Pooja ji, help ke liye."Agent: "Welcome Sir."

Agent: Hello, good afternoon. Mera naam Vivek hai aur main AXIS Finance se baat kar raha hu. Kya meri baat Mr. Rajendra Sharma se ho rahi hai?
Customer: Haan, main Rajendra Sharma bol raha hu. Bataiye kya hai?
Agent: Sir, aapka personal loan account number PNL789456, jiska Rs. 35,500 ka EMI due hai, uske settlement ke regarding call kiya tha. Last due date 15th of November thi.
Customer: Settlement? Kis settlement ki baat kar rahe ho aap? Aur kitni baar bataunga main aapko ki main is amount ko pay nahi karunga. Aur tum log ne na call kar kar ke mere dimag kharab kar diya hai. Roz ek hi baat, ek hi information. Main keh raha hu ki meri financial condition theek nahi hai aur upar se aap log har din naye naye agents se call karwa rahe ho. Main tang aa chuka hu isse.
Agent: Sir, main understand kar raha hu aapki situation. Lekin aapka account kafi overdue ho gaya hai aur bank ke policies ke hisab se humein contact karna padta hai. Aap bataiye kab tak payment kar paenge, koi partial payment hi kar dijiye filhaal.
Customer: Partial payment, full payment, kuch nahi hoga. Aur na main aap logon ke calls ka ab jawab dunga. Bahut ho gaya hai harassment. Meri baat dhyan se suniye. Agar abhi bhi aapke calls band nahi hue na, toh main legal action lunga. Already maine apne lawyer se baat kar li hai aur main consumer forum mein complaint file karunga. Aap meri file close kijiye aur jitni jaldi ho sake meri information ko update kar lijiye apne system mein. Agli baar agar aapka phone aaya toh woh seedha mere advocate ko jayega. Tum log jaante nahi ho kya karna hai.<interruption> Bas harass karna aata hai.
Agent: Sir, please aise mat boliye. Hum toh bas bank ke rules follow kar rahe hain. Main aapka concern team ko forward kar deta hu.
Customer: Forward kijiye ya jo bhi kijiye, mujhe is number pe koi call nahi aana chahiye. Aur is loan ko close karo. I am serious about the legal action.
Agent: Theek hai sir, main note kar leta hu aapki request.

Agent: Namaste, mera naam Anil hai aur main CreditSmart se baat kar raha hoon. Kya main Mr. Rohan Gupta se baat kar sakta hoon?
Customer: Haanji, main Rohan Gupta hi bol raha hoon. Kahiye kya kaam hai?
Agent: Rohan ji, aapne hamari company se ek personal loan liya tha jiska account number hai LOAN12345. Isme abhi tak 25,500 rupees outstanding dikh rahe hain, aur aapki due date 15 tareekh thi. Hum aapko usi ke regarding call kar rahe hain.
Customer: outstanding? Matlab aapke record mein kuch galat dikha raha hai, Anil ji. Maine toh 20,000 ka EMI pichle mahine ki 10 tareekh ko bhar diya tha. Uske baad toh bas kuch thousand bache the. Yeh 25,500 kaise ho sakte hain?
Agent: Rohan ji, mere paas system mein jo data hai, uske according aapka last payment 5,000 ka dikh raha hai 10 March ko. Aur uske pehle ke outstanding amounts, plus interest aur late fees, milakar abhi tak ka total 25,500 hi dikha raha hai. Aapne kis method se pay kiya tha pichle mahine?<interruption>
Customer: Toh system hi galat bata raha hai. Maine pura 20,000 rupees pay kiya tha, UPI se. Mere bank statement mein bhi dikhega. Yeh additional interest aur penalti, main kyo bhugatunga jab maine payment time par kar diya tha? Aap log bas aise hi add karte jaate ho.
Agent: Rohan ji, main samajh sakta hoon ki aapko lag raha hai ki kuch discrepancy hai. Kya aapke paas woh UPI transaction ID hai? Aur ek minute, main ek baar system mein double-check karta hoon ki kahi koi pending payment update toh nahi hui hai. Waise, kya aapne humari team se statement request kiya tha pehle?<interruption>
Customer: Nahi, request nahi kiya tha. Lekin aap ek kaam karo, aap mujhe poore loan ka detailed statement bhej do. E-mail pe bhej do, mere registered email ID pe. Tabhi main samjhunga ki yeh 25,500 kaisa calculation hai. Jab tak statement nahi aayega, main toh payment nahi kar paunga.
Agent: Theek hai, Rohan ji. Main aapke registered email ID par next 24 ghante mein aapke account ka detailed statement bhej deta hoon. Aap usko review kijiye, aur agar usme aapko still koi discrepancy lagti hai toh aap humein usi mail pe reply kar sakte hain ya wapas call kar sakte hain. Hum ise investigate karwayenge. Statement milne ke baad aap humein kab tak confirm kar payenge payment ke liye?
Customer: Jab main statement dekh loon aur verify kar loon, uske do din ke andar main clear kar dunga jo sahi amount hoga. Lekin bina statement dekhe, main abhi ek paisa bhi nahi pay karunga, theek hai? Aur haan, yeh faltu ki interest aur penalties ke liye main jimmedar nahi hounga agar meri taraf se koi galti nahi hai.<interruption> To aap mail bhejwa do jaldi.
Agent: Nishchit rahiye Rohan ji. Statement aapko mil jayega. Aur jo sahi amount hoga, hum usi par baat karenge. Dhanyawad aapka samay dene ke liye. Aapka din shubh ho.

Agent:"Hello, am I speaking with Mrs. Priya Sharma?"Customer:"Yes, this is Priya. Who is calling, please?"Agent:"Good morning, Mrs. Sharma. My name is Sameer from Bharat Finance. I am calling regarding your outstanding EMI payment for loan account number BFH012345. Your EMI of fifteen thousand five hundred rupees was due on the 28th of last month, and we haven't received it yet."Customer:"Oh, yes, I am aware of it, Sameer. Thank you for calling. I was actually about to call your team myself."Agent:"Alright, Mrs. Sharma. Is there any particular reason for the delay? We understand sometimes there might be unexpected issues, but it's important to clear the outstanding amount as soon as possible to avoid further late payment charges."Customer:"Yes, there is an issue, but it's not that I don't want to pay. My bank account, from which the EMI usually gets debited, has been put on hold. It's my savings account with National Bank."Agent:"On hold? Could you please elaborate, Mrs. Sharma? What is the reason for your account being on hold?"Customer:"Yes, the bank says there's some KYC document pending on my side. I had some old account details, and they want me to update my Aadhaar and PAN again. I've submitted the documents, but it takes a few days for them to process it. So right now, I cannot access funds or make any transactions from that account. Everything is stuck."Agent:"I understand, Mrs. Sharma. So, because of the bank's KYC hold, you're unable to make the payment. Is that correct? Have you been given an estimate of when the hold might be lifted?"Customer:"That's correct. They said maybe two or three more days. But honestly, it's very frustrating. I have the funds, the money is there in the account, but I cannot use it. So my hands are tied until the bank releases it. And this EMI is the first thing I need to pay once it's open."Agent:"Understood, Mrs. Sharma. This is certainly an operational blockage. Are there any other alternative payment methods you could consider in the meantime? For example, do you have another bank account, or perhaps you could use a UPI payment if that account is not linked to the blocked one, or maybe even a direct transfer from a relative's account?"Customer:"Well, Sameer, most of my funds are tied up in that main account. I don't really have another account with significant balance right now. And regarding UPI, it's also linked to the same main account, so that's also blocked. Customer: Aapka call abhi nahi lag sakta. Yeh phone band hai ya coverage area se bahar hai.

Mera budget puri tarah se bigad gaya hai. Abhi toh har mahine bas juggle hi karta rehta hoon ki kiski payment pehle karun, kiska baad mein. Meri monthly income se ab ye saari EMIs manage karna mushkil ho gaya hai. Mujhe thoda samay chahiye, ya phir kuch solution suggest kariye.<interruption>  Agent: Jee sir, main samajh gayi aapki problem. Aapke upar kaafi EMIs ka bojh hai, aur aap is EMI ko abhi manage nahi kar paa rahe hain. Theek hai, main aapki situation note kar leti hoon. Kya aap koi partial payment kar sakte hain ya abhi bilkul bhi nahi ho payega?<interruption>  Customer: Abhi toh bohot mushkil hai madam. Bas har mahine socha tha ki kuch adjust ho jaayega, but mushkil hai. Kuch restructure wagairaah ho sake toh batana, varna aise hi pareshaan rahoonga.<interruption>  Agent: Theek hai Mr. Sharma. Main aapki baat apni management tak pahunchati hoon aur hum aapko jaldi hi wapas contact karenge. Filhal, main Hardship – Overindebtedness mein apki file mark kar rahi hoon.<interruption>  Customer: Haan, please jaldi karna.<interruption>  Agent: Dhanyawad, Mr. Sharma, din shubh ho.

Agent: Good afternoon, sir. Am I speaking with Mr. Arjun Sharma regarding your outstanding loan account, number PL-234567? My name is Amit from ABC Finance. Customer: Yes, this is Arjun. Amit, before you start, can you please tell me what is the reason for this call again? I think I've already spoken to someone multiple times this week about the same thing. Agent: Sir, I understand your concern about call frequency, and I apologise for any inconvenience. We are reaching out regarding the settlement offer for your personal loan with an outstanding amount of Rs. 1,50,000, which was due since six months now, on March 15th. We sent you a notice also. We discussed a one-time settlement amount of Rs. 1,00,000 in our previous conversation, and I wanted to check if you've had a chance to consider it further. Customer: Amit, I have received your legal notice also, okay? And I have considered your offer, multiple times now. I already told your colleague last time that this one lakh is just not feasible for me. It's too high. Your people already made a proposal of seventy thousand, just last month. Why is it now suddenly one lakh? This is the issue I have, the interest and penalties have just spiralled out of control, this is not the real amount. Agent: Sir, the seventy thousand proposal might have been based on different calculations, or it could have expired. The current system-generated settlement for your account in NPA stage is one lakh. This amount includes a significant waiver of late fees and some interest, considering your financial situation. Customer: No, no, no, Amit. I clearly remember. We agreed on seventy thousand. I even got a confirmation email which stated the proposal for seventy thousand for full and final settlement. I was ready to pay then, had arranged the funds, but suddenly I received another call saying that proposal is not valid and you raised it to one lakh. How can I trust your new offer now when a previous, lower proposal, which I was ready to honour, was just cancelled by your company? So I cannot accept this new one lakh offer. It's just not right and it's definitely not what we had agreed upon earlier. It feels like you are going back on your word every time. Agent: Sir, I assure you we always strive for transparency. Sometimes there are system updates or internal approvals needed, which can lead to revision of offers. However, your feedback regarding the previous proposal is noted. So just to confirm, Mr. Sharma, you are unable to proceed with the Rs. 1,00,000 settlement offer today? Customer: That is correct, Amit. I am rejecting this settlement. I can't afford one lakh. That original seventy thousand proposal, maybe that was manageable, but not this. Unless you have another offer that is reasonable, there's nothing else to discuss. And please don't call me repeatedly, it's causing me a lot of trouble. Agent: Understood, Mr. Sharma. We'll update the records accordingly. I will ensure your concerns regarding call frequency are also logged. Thank you for your time, sir.

Agent: I understand. Can you tell me what's happening? When do you think you'll be able to make the payment?

Customer: <interruption> My father, he had a heart attack two weeks ago. He's still in the hospital in Delhi. I had to rush there immediately, and the medical bills... the ICU charges alone are running to almost 3 lakhs per day. I've been staying there with my mother, managing everything.

Agent: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that. That must be extremely stressful for you and your family. How is your father doing now?

Customer: He's stable, thank God, but the doctors say he needs to stay in the ICU for at least another week, maybe two. The hospital is asking for advance payment, and I've already used up most of my savings. My wife is also worried because we have the house EMI and now this... I just couldn't prioritize the loan payment right now.

Agent: That's completely understandable, Rajesh. Medical emergencies are beyond anyone's control. I can see you're in a difficult situation. Tell me, once your father is discharged and things settle down, when do you think you might be able to clear this outstanding amount? Your current dues are 38,750 rupees including the late fees.

Customer: I... I'm not sure right now. Maybe after another month or so? Once the hospital bills are settled and I can get back to my normal routine. My salary comes on the 25th, but most of it will go towards the medical expenses for the next few weeks.

Agent: I completely understand. This is a genuine hardship situation. Rather than putting pressure on you right now, let me see what options we have. Can I ask — do you have any support from other family members, or is this entirely on you?

Customer: My brother is helping a bit, but he has his own family. My mother is retired, so she can't contribute much. It's mostly on me and my wife's income. We're managing, but it's tight. Very tight.

Agent: Rajesh, I want to help you here. Given what you're going through, I'd like to escalate your case for a hardship assessment. This means we can look at options like a temporary payment moratorium or restructuring your EMI for a few months while you handle this medical emergency. You won't be in default, and we can work with you.

Customer: Really? You can do that? Because honestly, I want to pay, I really do. I'm not trying to avoid this, but right now every rupee is going to keep my father alive. I feel terrible about missing the payment.

Agent: I can absolutely hear that, and I want you to know that we recognize this is a genuine crisis, not a case of unwillingness to pay. What I need from you is to confirm your current address so I can process this escalation, and then I'll need you to provide some documentation — hospital discharge summary or bills, something that shows the medical emergency. Can you do that?

Customer: Yes, yes, I can send those. My address is still the same — Flat 302, Ashoka Apartments, Sector 12, Noida. I have all the hospital documents. When will I hear back about the moratorium?

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. I'll submit this for review today, and you should hear back within 2-3 business days. In the meantime, please don't worry about making the payment. Just focus on your father's recovery. Once we get approval, we'll send you the revised terms. Is this number the best way to reach you?

Customer: Yes, this number is fine. Thank you for understanding. I was really stressed about this call.

Agent: You're welcome. Take care of your family, and we'll be in touch very soon. All the best to your father's recovery.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, who is this? Kaun bol raha hai?

Agent: Sir, this is Priya from Collections Team at FinServe Finance. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4521. You have an outstanding amount of Rs. 47,300 due since 15th December. How are you doing today?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know, I know. Mujhe pata hai. What do you want? I'm busy right now.

Agent: Sir, I understand you're busy. This will just take two minutes. You've missed three EMI payments now. Your due amount is <interruption>

Customer: Listen, I don't care what amount you're saying. I never agreed to take this loan in the first place. The whole thing is wrong. Why are you people calling me again and again?

Agent: Sir, I can see here that the loan was disbursed in your name on 20th August, 2023. The EMI is Rs. 8,900 per month. Can we discuss a payment plan to help you clear this?

Customer: No, no, no. You listen carefully — I told the bank people already, I don't want to pay anything. The loan is not legitimate. I signed some documents but I never understood what they were for. Your company has made a mistake or you're trying to cheat me.

Agent: Sir, I understand your concern. Let me help you with this. If there's a documentation issue, we can definitely review it. But right now, if you could make a payment of at least Rs. 15,000 today, that would help us move forward <interruption>

Customer: Arey, are you listening to me or not? I said no! I'm not paying anything. Not today, not tomorrow, not ever. This is not my responsibility. You people keep calling and calling, it's harassment! I have already told three of your agents the same thing.

Agent: Sir, I appreciate your frustration. But the account is now 90 days past due. If we don't resolve this soon, the matter will go to our legal team. Can we at least set up a callback for next week? Maybe you can speak with a supervisor who can review your case <interruption>

Customer: No supervisor, no callback, nothing. I don't want to talk to anyone from your company anymore. Stop calling me. If you call again, I will file a complaint with the RBI. I'm warning you.

Agent: Sir, I understand. But before we end this call, let me just clarify — are you saying you completely refuse to pay this amount? Is there any hardship or issue preventing payment that we can help with?

Customer: I'm refusing because this loan should not exist. It's not my responsibility and I'm not paying. That's final. Don't call me again. Samjhe? Bas. Khatam.

Agent: Sir, I've noted your refusal. However, I must inform you that continued non-payment will result in legal proceedings. I'm escalating this to our legal team today.

Customer: Do whatever you want. I'm done talking.

<call disconnects>

Agent: Hello Kavitha Nair ji, main Meghna baat kar raha/rahi hoon Collections se.
Customer: Haan, suniye — mujhe settle karna hai yeh account. Batao kya best offer hai?
Agent: Kavitha Nair ji, aapka total outstanding 28,000 hai. Hum 15,400 rupees mein full and final settlement de sakte hain — one time payment.
Customer: 15,400 toh zyada hai mere liye. Honestly main maximum 19,600 de sakta/sakti hoon — woh bhi 15 din ka time chahiye arrange karne ke liye. Doosre lenders ke saath bhi negotiations chal rahi hain.
Agent: Kavitha Nair ji, 19,600 thoda high hai hamare liye accept karne ke liye. Main manager se discuss karta/karti hoon — ek middle ground nikaalte hain.
Customer: Theek hai, discuss karo. Lekin quickly — mera budget limited hai aur agar aap nahi maane toh main doosre lender ke saath pehle deal karunga/karungi.
Agent: Samjha/Samjhi. Main aaj shaam tak callback karunga/karungi confirmation ke saath.

Agent: Namaste! Main Rajesh bol raha hoon Indus Finance se. Kya main Rajesh Kumar se baat kar sakta hoon?

Customer: Haan, main hi bol raha hoon. Kya baat hai? Aapne itni baar call kiye hain is mahine mein.

Agent: Haan sir, actually aapke account ka outstanding balance abhi pending hai. EMI 15th ko due thi, aur aaj 28th ho gaya. Kya aap payment kar sakte ho?

Customer: Haan, main karna chahta hoon na payment, lekin ek problem hai. Mera bank account... wo freeze ho gaya hai, sir.

Agent: Account freeze? Matlab? Kya aap thode aur details de sakte ho?

Customer: Haan, to mera HDFC account, wo court ke order se frozen ho gaya hai. Mere wife ke saath kuch property dispute thi, aur court ne order de diya account ko freeze karne ka. Bank ne mujhe letter diya hai do hafta pehle.

Agent: Acha, samajh gaya. Toh abhi aap account se paise nikal nahi sakte?

Customer: Bilkul nahi, sir. Mujhe debit card se bhi kuch nahi mil raha. Aur ATM se bhi nahi. Bank ne kaha hai ki jab tak court order hata nahi deta, tab tak account block rahega. Maine soch tha ki maybe transfer kar doon doosre account se, lekin wife ke naam ka account hai wo bhi, aur woh abhi ghar par nahi hai.

Agent: Okay sir, main samajhta hoon. Toh aap payment karna chahte ho, lekin account freeze hai. Kya aap kisi aur tarike se payment kar sakte ho? Like NEFT transfer, ya cheque, ya kisi relative ke account se?

Customer: Arre, NEFT bhi to bank account se hi hota hai na. Aur cheque... haan, cheque ek option ho sakta hai, lekin mujhe abhi check book nahi hai. Wife ke paas check book hai, aur woh Monday ko ghar par aayengi.

Agent: Acha sir, to aap Monday ko check de sakte ho? Aur court order ke liye, aapne court mein appeal file ki hai ya kuch?

Customer: Haan, lawyer ne kaha hai ki appeal karunga, lekin ye sab process slow hai na. Court ko bhi time lagta hai. Lawyer ne kaha 2-3 mahine lag sakte hain court order reverse karne mein.

Agent: Samajh gaya, sir. Toh right now aapka account hold hai, aur aap Monday ko check de sakte ho. Kya aap committed ho sakte ho Monday ko payment ke liye? Full outstanding amount 47,500 rupees hai.

Customer: Haan, Monday ko check zarur dunga. But sir, kya aap mujhe extension de sakte ho? Kyunki court order ke wajah se mere credit score bhi affect ho raha hoga, aur financial situation thoda difficult hai.

Agent: Sir, account hold ke wajah se aap payment nahi kar paa rahe, to extension to mil jayega. Par check zaroori hai Monday ko. Aur aapka lawyer kya kah raha hai court order ke baare mein? Kya clear timeline hai?

Customer: Haan, lawyer ne kaha 2-3 mahine, shayad March tak clear ho jayega. Uske baad account unblock hoga aur paise nikal sakta hoon.

Agent: Bilkul sir. To aap Monday ko check de denge, aur hum court order ke baare mein update le sakte hain next week? Aur agar account unblock ho jaye, to immediately NEFT kar dena, haan?

Customer: Haan sir, bilkul. Monday ko check zarur dunga. Aur jaise hi court order clear hoga, main apna account unlock karwa lunga aur paise bhar dunga.

Agent: Perfect sir. Main aapke account mein note kar dunga — "Customer willing to pay, but account frozen due to court order. Check payment scheduled for Monday. Follow-up required post-court resolution." Aapka phone number 98765-43210 sahi hai na?

Customer: Haan, ye number sahi hai. Aur agar mujhe Monday tak court order ke baare mein update mil jaye, to main bata dunga.

Agent: Bilkul sir. Hum aapko Monday evening ko call karenge check payment confirm karne ke liye. Aur agar court order clear ho jaye, to aap directly inform kar dena. Kya ye sahi hai?

Customer: Haan, bilkul. Thank you sir.

Agent: Aapka swagat hai, sir. Have a good day!

Customer: Arrey, itna serious kya ho gaya? Woh cheque jo maine submit kiya tha, woh bounce toh ho gaya tha, lekin mera galti toh nahi tha na. Mere account mein balance hi nahi tha us time.

Customer: <interruption> Wait, wait. Ek minute. Itna extra charge? Ye toh bilkul unfair hai. Maine jo cheque submit kiya, wo bounce toh ho gaya, lekin mera toh koi galti hi nahi thi. Bank ne balance check nahi kiya kya?

Agent: Priya, main samajhta hoon aapka frustration, lekin ye bank ka standard rule hai. Cheque bounce hone par ye charges lagti hain. Customer: Re-present matlab kya? Woh cheque toh bounce ho gaya na?

Agent: Haan, woh cheque bounce ho gaya, lekin agar aapke account mein ab balance hai toh aap us cheque ko dobara submit kar sakte ho. Hum internally ye process kar denge aur 3-4 din mein cheque clear ho jayega. Aapka salary toh recent mein aa gaya na?

Customer: Theek hai, samajh gaya. Toh main apna original cheque leke branch mein jaunga aur re-presentation ke liye apply kar dunga. Lekin ek baat — kitne din mein clear ho jayega?

Agent: 3-4 din mein clear ho jayega. Branch mein aap re-presentation form fill kar dena aur woh original cheque number mention kar dena. Hum internally schedule kar denge. Aapka contact number abhi bhi 9876543210 hi theek hai na?

Agent: Bilkul, maine note kar liya. 8765432198 office number. Ab aap jab branch mein jao toh reference number mention kar dena. Aapka reference number hai — REP-2024-5521-PS. Yeh note kar lo.

Customer: REP-2024-5521-PS. Theek hai, note kar liya. Toh main kal morning hi branch chala jaunga. Ek minute — agar cheque clear ho gaya toh account fully settled ho jayega na? Kya aur kuch pending rahega?

Agent: Haan, cheque clear hone ke baad account settled ho jayega. Lekin aap ensure kar lena ki account mein sufficient balance ho. Agar cheque dobara bounce hua toh hum directly court mein case file kar denge. Samjha?

Customer: Samajh gaya. Balance toh sufficient hai. Kal morning branch chala jaunga. Aur agar koi issue aaye toh main call kar dunga.

Agent: Bilkul. Aapki cooperation ke liye dhanyavaad Priya. Ek aur baat — cheque submit karwane ke baad 4-5 din mein hum status update kar denge. Aur agar koi problem ho toh hum aapko office number par call kar denge. Kya sab kuch clear hai?

Customer: Theek hai Pooja ji. Main koshish karta hoon abhi. Dhanyawad.

transcript:
Agent: Hello Deepak Yadav ji, main Anand bol raha/rahi hoon Collections se.
Customer: Suno pehle — aap log kal mujhe 7 baar phone kar chuke ho. 7 baar! Yeh koi legal hai kya?
Agent: Deepak Yadav ji, main apologize karta/karti hoon agar zyada calls aaye.
Customer: Zyada nahi, unacceptable hai. Main jaanta/jaanti hoon ki RBI ke guidelines hain — ek din mein itne calls allowed nahi hain. Main already ek complaint draft kar raha/rahi hoon Banking Ombudsman ke liye. Mere lawyer ne bhi bola hai yeh harassment hai.
Agent: Deepak Yadav ji, main is matter ko compliance team ko immediately escalate kar raha/rahi hoon. Aapko harassment experience nahi hona chahiye tha.
Customer: Escalate karo. Aur main chahta/chahti hoon ek written apology bhi aur assurance ki aage se yeh nahi hoga. Tabhi payment ke baare mein baat hogi.
Agent: Ji bilkul. Main aaj hi complaint file kar deta/deti hoon aur aapko resolution ke baare mein inform karunga/karungi.
Customer: Theek hai. Record kar lena — main sab document kar raha/rahi hoon.

Agent: Hello, is this Hitesh Vora?
Customer: Yes yes, this is Hitesh Vora.
Agent: Hitesh Vora ji, calling regarding your vehicle loan account — 12,500 outstanding. Can I verify — date of birth on file?
Customer: Uh... it is... 12th March... 1988.
Agent: The date of birth on our record is different. Can you confirm which city the loan was taken in?
Customer: It was in... Delhi. No wait — Gurgaon. Yes Gurgaon.
Agent: Hitesh Vora ji, I am getting some inconsistency in your answers. For security I will need to pause this call and escalate for identity verification.
Customer: No no I am Hitesh Vora only. I just forgot the details.
Agent: I understand — but as a security measure I need to flag this. The actual account holder will receive a verification link on the registered number. Please do not make any payments until identity is confirmed.

Agent: Hello, is this Vikram Desai speaking?

Customer: Haan, yes, speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Vikram, this is Sanjana from Credence Finance. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 7834. Do you have a minute?

Customer: See, I don't know why you people keep calling. I'm telling you, this loan is closed na. Already I settled it. I paid the full amount last year itself.

Agent: Okay, okay. Let me just check the system here. You're saying it's closed and settled?

Customer: Yes yes, settled. We had some problem at that time, money was tight, so I went to the branch in Pune and we made agreement with manager. He said, okay, you pay forty-seven thousand rupees and that is finished. Loan is done. So I paid it, we got the certificate also from him.

Agent: Right. So you're saying you did a settlement payment of forty-seven thousand. When was this, Vikram?

Customer: It was in March 2024 na. March end only. I paid by cheque directly at the branch counter. The manager, he gave us the paper saying loan is closed. I still have it somewhere in my files.

Agent: I see. Let me just look at what the system is showing. <interruption> What I'm finding here is that the account is still marked as active, and there's still showing an outstanding balance of approximately fifty-nine thousand rupees.

Customer: No no no, that is not correct. Why it is showing like that? I paid the full amount. The settlement was approved and I paid. How can there be balance remaining?

Agent: I understand your frustration, Vikram. Let me ask — do you have that certificate document with you right now? Or do you remember the reference number or date?

Customer: The reference number I don't have in front of me, but it is there in the papers. The date, it was March 25th or 26th, around that time. I remember because my daughter's exam was happening. And the certificate, yes, I have it somewhere.

Agent: And when the manager said you pay forty-seven thousand and it is finished, did he mention that the remaining balance would be waived or adjusted?

Customer: Haan, that's what he said. The remaining amount, the manager said it will be written off. So the total debt, it is cleared with that forty-seven thousand. That's what I understood from him. He said no more to pay.

Agent: Okay, so according to what you're telling me, there was a settlement arrangement where you paid forty-seven thousand as a one-time payment, and the rest would be waived. And you paid this by cheque at the Pune branch. Is that right?

Customer: Yes, exactly that. I don't understand why your system is still showing money outstanding. Maybe the cheque is bouncing or something? Or maybe the system is not updated? But I definitely paid. You can check with the Pune branch people.

Agent: That's a very fair point. What I'm going to do is escalate this to our settlement verification team and request them to check with the Pune branch directly. We need to confirm if the cheque was received and cleared, and if the settlement file is available. <interruption> This I cannot resolve on this call, but we will definitely sort it out for you.

Customer: Okay, yes please check. Because I should not be getting collection calls if the loan is already settled and closed. This is causing me stress only, you know.

Agent: Absolutely, and I apologize for the inconvenience. Let me flag this as priority. Can I get an email address so we can send you the findings once we verify?

Customer: Okay, it is vikram.desai82 at gmail dot com.

Agent: Perfect. I have noted that. Vikram, we will contact you within five to seven working days with what we find. In the meantime, the system is now marked as under review. You should not receive any further collection calls during this verification period. And once we confirm the settlement, we will issue you a revised statement and close the account properly.

Customer: Okay, but I want to make sure my credit report is corrected also. If the loan is already closed, why is it still showing active?

Agent: That is a valid concern. Once we confirm the settlement and closure in our records, we will work to update your credit bureau report as well. For now, your account is flagged as under review pending settlement verification. Okay?

Customer: Alright. So I should expect to hear from you within a week?

Agent: Yes, within five to seven working days. We will be in touch. Is this the best number to reach you?

Customer: Yes, this number is fine.

Agent: Thank you, Vikram. I have everything noted down. We will contact you soon with an update.

Customer: Okay, thank you.

Agent: You're welcome. Goodbye.

Customer: Goodbye.

Agent: Namaste Rakesh Kumar ji? Main XWZ Finance se baat kar rahi hoon. Aapka loan account number XXXXXX hai na?
Customer: Ji, Rakesh Kumar bol raha hoon. Kya baat hai?
Agent: Ji sir, aapka EMI amount ₹3,850, jo ki 5th June ko due tha, abhi tak receive nahi hua hai. Aapko ek reminder call ke liye contact kiya gaya hai.
Customer: Haan, madam, mujhe pata hai. Main actually subah se try kar raha hoon payment karne ka, mere account mein funds hain. Lekin UPI payment nahi ho paa raha hai, baar baar failed ho jaa raha hai. Net banking bhi try kiya, wahan bhi transaction अटक raha hai.
Agent: Achha, UPI se problem aa rahi hai? Konsi bank ka account hai sir aapka?

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Customer: See, Priya, I want to pay, I really do. But the situation is... it's very difficult right now. We had the floods, na? Agent: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that, Rajesh. That must be extremely stressful. Can you tell me a bit more about the impact on your business? Are you still able to operate?

Customer: <interruption> No, no, the warehouse is completely damaged. The building itself — the walls, the roof — everything needs repair. And the stock, Priya, the stock was worth almost 8 lakhs. I have lost everything. Right now I am trying to get insurance claims processed, but you know how slow that is. The surveyor came last week, but the claim will take at least two to three months to settle.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. This is clearly a major external disruption to your business. Have you been able to generate any income since the floods, or is the business completely halted?

Customer: Completely halted. I cannot operate from that location anymore. I am looking for an alternative warehouse space, but that also requires capital which I don't have right now. My wife is very worried. We have been living off our savings, but that is also running out. I have not paid my own house rent for the last month because of this situation.

Agent: Rajesh, I can hear the stress in your voice, and I want to help you find a solution. Before we discuss options, let me ask — do you have any timeline on when the insurance claim might come through? Or any other source of funds that might help in the near term?

I am hoping to restart operations in a smaller space within the next month or so, but I need capital for that.

Agent: Okay, so you are looking at a one to three month window before you can stabilize your cash flow again. Is that fair to say?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. One month minimum, maybe two or three months to get back to normal operations and start generating income again.

Customer: Okay, okay. How long will the approval take?

Customer: <interruption> Fifty thousand? Priya, I don't have that kind of cash right now. I am literally managing day-to-day expenses with what little savings I have left. I cannot commit to that amount.

Agent: That is very helpful, Rajesh. So you are committing to Rs. 10,000 by next week, and you will submit the moratorium request with documentation by then as well. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, yes. I will send the photos and the insurance claim form by tomorrow itself. And I will try to arrange the 10,000 by next Friday.

Agent: Hello, kya main Kiran Patil ji se baat kar sakta/sakti hoon?

Agent: Hello, good morning. Am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar? This is Priya calling from Lakshmi Finance regarding your loan account LF-2024-087654.

Customer: Yes, yes, this is Rajesh. But listen, I cannot talk right now. Things are very bad at home.

Agent: I understand, sir. I just need a few minutes. Your EMI of rupees 8,500 was due on the 10th of this month and we have not received payment yet. It is now the 18th. Can you please tell me when you will be able to pay?

Customer: Priya, I... <interruption> my father, he had a major heart attack last week. He is still in the hospital in Delhi. ICU, you know. I had to rush there immediately with my mother. We spent almost two lakhs already on the surgery and the medicines are so costly.

Agent: Oh, I am very sorry to hear that, sir. That must be very stressful for you and your family. Is he stable now?

Customer: Stable, yes, but he needs to stay in the hospital for at least two more weeks. The doctors said so. My mother is with him and I am here managing things, but my mind is completely... <interruption> how can I think about EMI when my father is fighting for his life? I have already used all my savings. I took a loan from my brother also.

Agent: I completely understand, Rajesh. Medical emergencies are very difficult. Tell me, what is your current situation? Do you have any funds available right now, or when do you think you might be able to make a payment?

Customer: Nothing available right now. My salary comes on the 25th, but even that I have to send to my mother for his hospital bills. The total bill is coming to almost four lakhs. I don't know how I will manage all the EMIs after this — I have two more loans also.

Agent: I see. So you have other loan obligations as well. Rajesh, I want to help you. We can look at some options. First, can you confirm your current address? Is it still Plot 42, Sector 7, Chandigarh?

Customer: Yes, that is correct. But Priya, I am telling you, right now I cannot commit to any payment date. My father's health is unpredictable. I need at least three weeks to get some clarity. Can you just hold the account or something?

Agent: I hear you, sir. Let me note down what you have shared — your father is hospitalised, you have immediate medical expenses, and you are managing multiple loan obligations. This is definitely a hardship situation. What I would like to do is escalate this to our hardship assessment team. They can look at your account and possibly offer you some relief options like a payment moratorium for two to three months or a restructure of your EMI.

Customer: Really? That is possible? Because right now I feel like I am drowning. I cannot focus on work, I cannot sleep properly.

Agent: Yes, absolutely. These options exist for exactly this kind of situation. I will send you an email with the hardship application form. You will need to provide some supporting documents — your father's hospital discharge summary or medical bills, and proof of your salary. Can you do that?

Customer: I can do that. But how long will this take? And will there be any penalty for not paying now?

Agent: The assessment usually takes five to seven working days. I will flag your account as high priority given the medical emergency. As for penalties, let me check... <interruption> yes, I can see a late fee of 500 rupees has been applied, but once your hardship case is approved, we can review that as well. The main thing right now is to get you the relief you need.

Customer: Okay, okay. That sounds better. So I send the documents and then you people will decide?

Agent: Exactly. I am sending the form to your email right now. The email will be from our hardship@lakshmifinance.com. Please fill it out and attach the documents we discussed — hospital bills, discharge summary, and your recent salary slip. Once we receive it, our team will review and contact you within seven days with the outcome.

Customer: Thank you, Priya. I really appreciate this. I was very worried you would just keep pressuring me for payment.

Agent: Not at all, Rajesh. Our role is to help you find a sustainable solution, not to add to your stress during such a difficult time. Is there anything else you need from me right now?

Customer: No, I think that is it. I will send the documents tomorrow or the day after. My father is improving slightly, so maybe I can focus a bit better.

Agent: That is good news. Please do send them as soon as you can. In the meantime, if your father's situation changes or if you have any questions about the form, you can call us. But we will not pressure you for payment until the assessment is complete. Take care of yourself and your family.

Customer: Thank you. I will be in touch.

Agent: Thank you for speaking with me, Rajesh. We will be here to help. Goodbye.

Customer: Haan, 25th ko salary aa jayegi to main 26th ko payment kar dunga. Aur IMPS se bhi ek baar try kar lunga aaj shaam ko.

Agent: Perfect. Main note kar dunga — Vikram, loan account 4782, commitment 18,500 rupees on 26th after salary. Aur aaj shaam 6 baje IMPS attempt karna. Agar koi issue ho to call kar dena, mera extension 2451 hai. Theek?

Customer: Haan, bilkul. Shukrya bhai.

Agent: Welcome. Take care.

transcript: Agent: Good afternoon, am I speaking to Mr. Rajesh Kumar?Customer: <sighs> Haanji, haan, that's me. Who is this?Agent: Mr. Kumar, my name is Vikram from XYZ Finance. Calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 12345. Your EMI of twelve thousand five hundred rupees, due on May fifth, is still showing outstanding. Uhm, also, we need to clarify a field visit from yesterday. Our executive, Mr. Sharma, reported a visit to your registered address at Two, Ashoka Towers. His GPS-tagged visit was logged yesterday, June tenth, at 4:35 PM, with coordinates 19.0760 North, 72.8777 East. Could you please confirm if you met him, ya agar aap ne baat ki thi unse?Customer: Listen, this is just too much, boss! Kya hai yeh, haan? Every day you call, like, four, five times? Aur ab, abhi ghar pe bhi banda bhej diya aapne? I spoke to your agent, okay? Kal shaam ko woh aaye the, haan, main mila unse. Lekin I already told the previous agent on the phone that I'll clear it, no? Aur that legal notice you sent also... maine bola I will resolve. Why all this harassment?Agent: My apologies for the repeated outreach, Mr. Kumar. The field visit and follow-up calls are part of our escalation process when an account, like yours, is significantly overdue and we're unable to confirm the payment commitment through regular calls. Since your identity is confirmed, and you also received the legal notice, may I please understand what is causing this consistent delay? Why was the May fifth payment missed?Customer: Dekho, personal issues, thode complications the, isliye delay hua. Bas that's all. And yes, yesterday, your field agent, Mr. Sharma, he also clearly explained to me. He said agar abhi payment nahi hota hai, then I need to visit your branch, uh, latest by this Thursday to sort out a proper payment plan. Maine unko "yes" bola hai, okay? Maine agreement diya hai. Now please, I don't want any more calls, no more visits. It's really frustrating, yaara.Agent: Alright, Mr. Kumar, I have noted your concern regarding the call frequency, and I'll update the records accordingly. So, just to be absolutely clear for our internal closure, you confirm you will be visiting our XYZ Finance Mumbai Central branch this Thursday, June thirteenth, to settle this matter? This commitment is to physically appear at the branch, right?Customer: Haan, haan, pakka. This Thursday, June thirteenth. I will definitely come to the branch. Just ensure these continuous calls and visits stop, please. Bas, that's it. No more nuisance.Agent: Thank you for the confirmation, Mr. Kumar. We appreciate your cooperation. I am updating your account notes regarding your commitment to visit the branch on June thirteenth. We look forward to seeing you then. Good bye.Customer: Hmm, bye.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Fintech Collections. I'm calling regarding your loan account with us — account number ending in 4782. Do you have a few minutes to speak?

Customer: Arre, I know, I know. I've been meaning to call you people. The thing is, I had some issues last month with my business, but now things are getting better. What is the exact amount I owe right now?

Agent: Of course, Rajesh. Your current outstanding balance is Rs. 47,500, and this was due on the 15th of this month. We're now on the 22nd, so there's a late fee of Rs. 2,100 that has been added. So the total amount due is Rs. 49,600.

Customer: Okay, okay. That's fine. I can manage that. Actually, my salary comes on the 25th — that's just three days from now. I will pay the full amount on the 25th itself. You can note that down.

Agent: That's excellent, Rajesh. I'm very glad to hear that. Just to confirm — you're committing to pay the full outstanding amount of Rs. 49,600 on the 25th of this month, correct? That's three days from today?

Customer: Yes, yes, 25th. Full amount. I will transfer it through NEFT from my account. No problem at all. My salary always comes on the 25th, and I will clear this immediately.

Agent: Perfect. And just to verify, Rajesh — the payment will be made to the account details we have on file, yes? The NEFT details are in the SMS we sent you last week.

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, I have that message. I will do the transfer on the 25th morning itself. No delay.

Agent: Wonderful. I'm logging your commitment now. Full payment of Rs. 49,600 by the 25th of this month via NEFT. Rajesh, I want to thank you for being cooperative. We'll send you a confirmation SMS with the payment details and a reminder on the 25th morning. If for any reason there's a delay, please call us immediately, okay?

Customer: Haan, no problem. I will definitely pay on the 25th. You don't need to worry. My business is back on track now, and I want to clear this loan quickly. Thank you for understanding.

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. We appreciate your commitment. Your account is now marked as Promise to Pay for the 25th. Have a good day.

Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.
Customer: Aapka call abhi nahi lag sakta. Yeh phone band hai ya coverage area se bahar hai.
Aapka call abhi nahi lag sakta kyunki jis subscriber ko aap call kar rahe hain, ve vyast hain.

Agent: Hello, mein Rahul baat kar raha hoon XYZ Finance se. Kya meri baat Rajeev Sharma ji se ho rahi hai?Customer: Haan ji, mein Rajeev Sharma bol raha hoon. Kya ho gaya? Aap logon ke kitne calls aate hain ek din mein!Agent: Sharma ji, sorry for the calls. Hum aapko aapke outstanding personal loan account number PNL54321 ke liye contact kar rahe hain. Aapki EMI 22 April ko due thi aur abhi tak clear nahi hui hai. Total outstanding abhi Rs. 85,000 ho gaya hai, jisme late fees bhi included hai. Mid Bucket mein aa gaya hai account. Kya aap payment aaj process kar sakte hain?Customer: Rahul ji, dekho mein aapko seedhi baat bataata hoon. Jab tak aap log mera CIBIL score theek nahi karwaoge na, mein ek bhi paisa nahi bharunga. Tum logon ne galat information feed ki hui hai bureau mein.Meri profile 'settled' dikha raha hai.Maine toh kabhi loan settle kiya hi nahi! Aap log ye theek karwao, uske baad hi kuch payment ki baat hogi. Maine ek naya car loan apply kiya tha, woh reject ho gaya because of your incorrect CIBIL reporting. This is not fair!Agent: Sir, hum aapki concern samajh rahe hain. Par payment karne ke baad hi hum CIBIL team ko request daal sakte hain. Agar aap abhi payment kar denge, toh hum immediate request daalenge correction ke liye. Aap Rs. 85,000 clear kar sakte hain kya aaj?Customer: Are Rahul ji, mein aapko clearly bol raha hoon! Maine apni identity confirm kar di, aur mein hi Rajeev Sharma bol raha hoon. Jo bhi maine bola, theek hai, woh wahi baat hai. Jab tak CIBIL report correct nahi hogi, usmein 'settled' dikhna band nahi hoga, tab tak main payment nahi karunga. Meri priority pehle woh CIBIL ka issue hai. Kya matlab, maine time pe bhara hai, aur phir bhi aapne galat report kiya. Aur ab due bata rahe ho? Ab tak 60 days cross ho gaye na, because of your mistake! Meri ek request hai ki pehle ye bureau records theek karo. Yehi hai meri condition, warna main koi payment nahi karunga.Agent: Theek hai, sir. Toh aapka kehna hai ki aapka CIBIL report mein incorrect status hai jisko aap pehle correct karwana chahte hain aur tabhi aap payment karenge. Main aapka yeh grievance escalate karwa deta hoon concerned team ko for verification and correction request. Please allow 3-5 working days for the team to look into it. Mein aapko tab tak next Tuesday update deta hoon. Lekin uske baad aap payment karenge na, jab issue resolve ho jayega?Customer: Haan, han, jab report theek ho jayegi aur confirm ho jayega, tab kar dunga payment. Par please jaldi karwana, aur itne calls bhi mat karna. Bas.Agent: Okay, sir. Thank you for confirming. I will update this interaction as a CIBIL dispute and will call you on Tuesday for an update. Apne side se main yeh escalate karva deta hoon. Thank you.

Agent: Namaste, kya main Priya Sharma se baat kar sakta hoon? Yeh Fintech Collections se call hai.

Customer: Haan, main hi hoon. Kya baat hai? Mujhe pata hai ki payment pending hai.

Agent: Bilkul, Priya ji. Aapke account mein 52,300 rupees outstanding hai jo 18th March ko due tha. Aaj 25th March hai. Kya aap payment kar sakte ho?

Customer: Haan, haan, main kar dunga na. Actually kal raat ko maine UPI se payment karne ki koshish ki tha, lekin... arre, transaction fail ho gaya. Mera Google Pay mein paise the, balance sufficient tha, lekin jab confirm kiya toh likha tha "Transaction Failed – Please Try Again Later." Phir maine doosri baar try kiya, same problem. Dekho, mera side se toh sab theek tha.

Agent: Achcha, toh aap payment karna chahte ho lekin UPI se problem aa raha hai? Kya error message dikha tha exactly?

Customer: Haan, yaar, bas likha tha transaction failed. Mera account mein paise the na, toh mujhe samajh nahi aaya ki kya problem tha. Phir maine NEFT se bhi try kiya tha, lekin woh bhi... <interruption>woh bhi fail ho gaya. Mera HDFC account se. Toh maine socha ki maybe aapke side se koi issue hai payment gateway mein.

Agent: <interruption>Nahi nhi, aapke side se nahi. Dekho, yeh payment gateway ka temporary outage ho sakta hai ya HDFC ke server mein koi glitch. Lekin aapka intent clear hai — aap payment karna chahte ho, bas technical problem aa raha hai. Toh hum aapko alternate option de sakte hain, na?

Customer: Haan, please. Mujhe kya karna chahiye? Aapke paas kaunsa option hai?

Agent: Toh dekho, aapke paas do-teen options hain. Ek toh aap direct NEFT kar sakte ho — mein aapko account details de dunga. Ya phir aap net banking se transfer kar sakte ho. Ya ek aur option — aap apne HDFC branch mein jaao aur cash deposit kar do. Kaunsa aapke liye easy hai?

Customer: Net banking se try kiya tha, woh bhi nahi hua. Lekin NEFT se kar dunga, haan. Mujhe account number de do. Aur kab tak kar dunga? Kal morning mein kar dunga?

Agent: Bilkul, kal morning mein kar sakte ho. Aapka account number 7392015847 hai, IFSC code FINC0001234. Amount 52,300 rupees. Aur ek baat — agar kal NEFT se payment ho jaye, toh 24 ghante mein aapke account mein reflect ho jayega. Kya aap confirm kar sakte ho ki kal morning mein payment kar denge?

Customer: Haan, haan, kal morning mein hi kar dunga. Lekin ek baat aur — agar yeh NEFT bhi fail ho gaya toh? Kya hoga? Mujhe toh payment karna hi hai na.

Agent: Agar NEFT fail ho jaye, toh aap mujhe immediately call kar dena. Mein aapko cheque option de dunga ya phir aap branch mein directly cash deposit kar sakte ho. Lekin NEFT usually safe hota hai, dekho. Aur agar payment ho gaya, toh aap mujhe confirmation de dena, okay?

Customer: Okay, bilkul. Kal morning mein NEFT kar dunga aur phir aapko message kar dunga ya call kar dunga.

Agent: Perfect, Priya ji. Toh aapka commitment hai ki aap kal 26th March ko NEFT se 52,300 rupees payment kar denge. Agar kisi reason se fail ho jaye, toh aap mujhe immediately call kar denge. Aur payment successful hone ke baad aap confirmation de denge. Kya yeh sab theek hai?

Customer: Haan, bilkul theek hai. Aur agar payment ho gaya toh mera account clear ho jayega na?

Agent: Haan, payment ho gaya toh aapka outstanding amount zero ho jayega aur account clear ho jayega. Koi aur pending nahi hoga. Toh kal morning mein NEFT kar dena, okay?

Customer: Okay, thank you. Kal kar dunga.

Agent: Thank you, Priya ji. Aapka cooperation ke liye dhanyavaad. Agar koi problem ho toh mujhe call kar dena. Have a good day.
